notes.title: Paint by numbers update!
notes.notes:
You can now generate a paint by numbers template from your own images and any image you find online! Vermillion will generate the outlines, which you can show above or below the paint on the canvas. The palette will be automatically filled with the required colors, between 2 and 20. You can change how detailed you want the outlines to be. You can isolate outlines to one color at a time, so you can very easily apply the right color in the right area. Painting has never been more accessible! 

Additionally, you can now open local images on the floating screen directly from inside Vermillion, which you can also use to generate paint by numbers templates.

As always, if you're enjoying the update, please consider leaving a review! Greatly appreciated. Have fun! 🙏🏻

notes.title: Gallery & Glossy paint update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, I've been hard at work on the Quest MR update, and I'm passing the savings onto [i]you[/i]! 

[list]
[*]You can now mount your paintings in the Manor and Loft studios by approaching a wall, and even have them sitting in a customizable frame.
[*]The paint now looks a whole lot glossier. It's pretty damn tasty if you ask me. You can still reduce or disable the specular highlight using the slider on the lamp, but will you want to? I think not.
[*]The painting settings have moved to a little panel on the palette, where you can now set the canvas mixing sensitivity, paint thickness, and an all new infinite paint toggle. I've revamped the canvas mixing sensitivity at 0 to properly never mix with what was on the canvas. With the mixing sensitivity at 0 and the infinite paint toggle enabled you can doodle away at your heart's content!
[*]You can grab anything from a distance now, so you don't have to reach and stretch or bump into the real world.
[*]I've fixed the hands being the wrong way around if you're starting in OpenVR as a leftie. Sorry about that!
[*]I've changed the two inch brush to have a smoother look to its paint. 
[*]A dry palette knife is now an excellent tool for smoothing paint on the canvas. Try it, it's something else.
[/list]

If you're enjoying the update, please leave a store review! That really helps out. Thanks!

notes.title: Overlay, Locomotion, Outdoor studio & OpenVR update
notes.notes:
The overlay is now out of beta! Have fun painting in any VR game. Remember that you need a powerful system to run two VR games simultaneously. You can always lower the SteamVR render resolution to gain performance!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=udc1i97KPLY

Another important change this update brings is improved locomotion. Locomotion was always a second class citizen in Vermillion, but this is no longer the case.
[list]
[*]Better teleport
[*]Smooth locomotion
[*]Snap, quick, and smooth rotation
[*]Grab locomotion (very useful to position yourself just right!)
[/list]
The smooth locomotion options are especially useful in overlay mode!

One more cool addition this update brings is a new outdoor studio. You know, in case you're done painting in Skyrim or VRChat.

The final important change this update brings is that now the default VR runtime is OpenVR, instead of OpenXR. OpenXR is the supposed new standard, but it's been nothing but trouble since Vermillion's launch. To this day it causes some users' controllers to not track. Out with the new, in with the old! You can still use the OpenXR launch option to bypass SteamVR on non-SteamVR platforms, such as Oculus and WMR.

Artwork by @lizaledwards!

notes.title: The Midnight Oil Update
notes.notes:
I know a lot of you like the burn the midnight oil when painting, so here's an update to cater for that. Now there's a nighttime and a dawn/dusk variant of the two studio environments, making Vermillion a whole lot easier on the eyes (and the mind) when you're not painting in broad daylight. The update also comes with a visual upgrade, with a soft shadow cast by the canvas so the easel doesn't stick out when painting at night, and nicer reflections on the floor as well. Enjoy!

As always, if you haven't yet, it really helps out if you leave a review. Thanks!

Edit: There's actually a few extra features that I totally forgot to list!

[list]
[*]The projector transparency slider is now always visible on the side of the painting.
[*]You can instantly toggle the projection off and on by pressing down on the brush hand thumb stick / center of the Vive track pad.
[*]The active layer is saved alongside the painting now, so you won't accidentally resume on the wrong layer.
[*]Added a new paint along playlist by Brian Sloan.
[*]Fixed the ambient occlusion of the backside of the canvas showing through on the studio photo export.
[*]Layer thumbnails on the layer page are now no longer affected by lighting.
[/list]

notes.title: The Big Update
notes.notes:
The big update is live! These are all the changes I've been working on the past months for the Quest release. 

[list]
[*]The painting mechanics have been improved, removing common artifacts while painting.
[*]The paint thinner has been improved. Note that paint can no longer be thickened up again by adding opaque paint on the palette, to make it easier to maintain a constant opacity. You can add more thinner by loading more thinner from the bucket and going back to the palette.
[*]There's a completely new easel, which is far more flexible. It can be folded flat so you can rest your hand on a table, or even turned upside down so you can paint lying down. There's a new grip on the mixing tray as well, allowing you to move and rotate the entire easel, making it easier to get it just right instead of having to rely on teleporting.
[*]The brushes, brush and palette stand had a makeover.
[*]There's two new brushes: a dagger brush (both smooth and rough variants), and a silicone dagger color shaper, both scalable. Try using the latter to move paint around on the canvas!
[*]The short flat brushes are now fully scalable.
[*]The rag now has a single tip, and has pressure based wiping. Dip the rag in paint thinner to fully erase paint.
[*]The palette knife now needs to be tilted to create the stipple pattern, rather than it being pressure based.
[*]Added a lamp on the easel, with which you can turn off the glare on the canvas.
[*]The Manor studio has been refurbished.
[*]A new studio has been added, a whitewall loft.
[*]Vermillion is now localized in German, Spanish, Italian, French, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
[*]You now have 20 canvas undos instead of 5. The undos are also a lot more granular, happening after every slight change instead of grouping several daubs together.
[*]The palette and mixing tray are saved alongside the painting, so you can always get back to painting without having to remix colors.
[*]Paint on the palette is glossier, removing the glare, and looking quite shiny at the right angle.
[*]New web browser.
[/list]

Bug fixes:
[list]
[*]The correct OpenXR runtime is now chosen behind the scenes, instead of making you do it.
[*]Fixed LIV not teleporting correctly.
[*]Made it easier to beat the devil out of the brushes.
[/list]

Since this is a major update, it's not unlikely that there's some issues. Let me know on the forums or on Discord if you run into any problems! https://vermillion-vr.com/discord

notes.title: Preview the new update in the public beta!
notes.notes:
I've been porting Vermillion to Quest these past months, and I'm passing the savings onto [i]you[/i]! If you join the public preview beta, you can test the new visuals, performance upgrades, all-new browser, and most importantly, the new easel. The easel can fold flat horizontally, and go a lot lower than the original. This allows you to rest your brush hand or arm while painting. I'll also allow it to be moved and turned like you already can with the brush and palette stand.

To join the pubic beta, right click Vermillion in your Steam library > Properties > Betas > Select "preview". I'll be adding updates in the coming days. Let me know what you think in the Steam community or on Discord! https://discord.com/invite/Aw2zKxz

notes.title: The Impasto Update + G2 support
notes.notes:
Impasto? Yeah, I could eat. Or rather, impasto is the effect of using very thick paint on the canvas to create a textured look. I have updated the paint visuals to be much thicker, giving you the option to create rich texture on your canvas. If you like to keep it flat, you can always use less paint, flatten the thick paint with any tool, or use the slider in Settings > Painting. While this in itself is a great new feature, the main driver behind it was the ability for achieving better Bob Ross style foliage - i.e. tapping in happy little bushes. The two inch brush is now rounded, the one inch oval brush doesn't leave a circle mark, and tapping in leaves and bushes gives you a very nice textured look, rather than the sort of rectangular muddiness you've had up to now when using the 2 inch. Try tapping in leaves with a fully loaded 2 inch (look at the pressure indicator) to see what I mean!

Your old paintings will not automatically show thicker paint. You can scale it up in the settings.

Additional changes:

- Reverb G2 controllers are now functional in the base Steam version, without having to switch to the system default OpenXR branch.
- Bristle (rough) variant of the one inch oval brush.
- Classic fan brush is back, since it allows smoother blending on things such as skin.
- Clicking a save thumbnail does not automatically open the last save, but shows all thumbnails instead.
- Palette knife scratching strength reduced again to what it was before last update.
- Fixed some brushes not being able to paint over some parts of the canvas.
- Several smaller bug fixes.

notes.title: The Crimson Update
notes.notes:
By popular request, I've made the default palette the complete Bob Ross landscape colors set.

I have adjusted the color model to allow for darker reds - this change will only happen in new paintings. Your old paintings are unaffected.

When using higher pressure with the 2 inch, the bristly pattern is no longer visible, allowing for smoother blends.

Improved the fan brush pattern to be more bristly, so it should be easier to get natural looking pine trees.

Added censored mode for the browser for spectators.

The brush sounds now fade out smoothly rather than cutting off harshly when no longer making contact with a surface / paint thinner.

Fixed the rag being able to load paint thinner. Shoutout to Harrier for reporting this!

I have removed the ticking sound for the spectator camera UI, since it was distracting when mixing paint on the canvas.
